page: Microsoft Azure B4pls_v2 is an entry-tier, burstable virtual machine instance based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. It is powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, configured with 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 8.0 GB total, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache structures include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic hardware acceleration is supported via AES flags, though advanced vector and matrix extensions are absent. The instance includes no bundled local storage and provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on external attached storage and network provisioning.

Benchmark results demonstrate variable compute throughput consistent with its burstable credit-based profile. In stress-ng testing, the instance reaches 1822.19 in single-core and 7243.95 in multi-core metrics, situating raw execution in the middle 50% band. However, memory-intensive and instruction-heavy suites show lower relative output, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1099.0 and multi-core score of 3672.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 48.64 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 29.1 GB/sec for writes, both ranking in the middle tier, whereas cached small-block bandwidth (283.03 GB/sec) and PassMark memory operations (1078.78) sit in the lower quartile. Static web delivery throughput achieves 5.73 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations deliver 5.65 million operations per second.

The hardware configuration trades sustained high-end performance for resource economy. By utilizing energy-efficient ARM cores and a burstable hypervisor scheduling model on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance offers cost-efficient compute capacity for non-continuous demands. It is suited for workloads that experience idle periods punctuated by bursts of activity, such as code staging, low-traffic web serving, microservices, internal development tools, and lightweight batch automation.
description: Microsoft Azure B4pls_v2 is a burstable ARM64 virtual machine powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. The instance supplies 4 vCPUs mapped across 4 single-threaded physical cores, complemented by 8.0 GB of system memory, or 2.0 GB per vCPU. Bundled local storage is absent, necessitating network-attached storage volumes for file systems. Benchmark evaluations place raw multi-core compute in the mid-range via stress-ng (7243.95), while Geekbench (3672.0 multi-core) and PassMark suites reflect lower per-core throughput on complex instruction sets. Large-block memory transfers achieve 48.64 GB/sec read and 29.1 GB/sec write bandwidth. Because the burstable CPU model balances lower baseline compute costs against intermittent spikes, the server is matched for intermittent background tasks, staging environments, low-traffic web servers, and lightweight containerized workloads.
